label: Wherever things are more and less in some perfection, there is…, by Well-founded-induction
meaning: Derives the quarta via's grades-to-maximum step (weak IsMaximumIn) from four nonlogical premises and excluded middle by well-founded induction along distinct causes of the perfection. The exceeding comparand has the perfection; a bearer that nothing exceeds is the maximum; a bearer that something exceeds has the perfection from a distinct cause, which is more such than it and so has the perfection, and the induction applies to that cause. The maximum is neither unique nor greatest, nor shown to cause anything, and is not identified with God. Cause-more-such is the existing unrestricted strengthening of Met II.1, stated without a synonymy condition by Posterior Analytics I.2, 72a29-30; exceeded-is-caused is stated by SCG II.15 n.3 (what belongs to something less than to others belongs to it from another cause) and supported by ST I q.44 a.1; no infinite regress of causes of a perfection is an unattributed strengthening of the species-scoped regress denials of In Metaph. II lect. 2 n. 11 and the secunda via, which support but do not state it. This is a formal derivation, not a reading of the source's order of argument: Aquinas grounds the step in approach to a maximum, not in causal ascent.
